cards.text: Quick catch-up, friend. Uzziah, king of Judah, walked into the temple of the LORD to burn incense, which only the priests were consecrated to do, and leprosy broke out right on his forehead. He lived cut off until the day he died, while his son Jotham ran the palace and governed the people.
Now Jotham is king at twenty-five years old, and his mother is Jerushah, daughter of Zadok. Twenty-five and running a KINGDOM, while it takes me three tries just to set an oven timer.

cards.question: King Jotham reigns in Jerusalem for ___ years.

cards.text: So how does Jotham do? He does what's right in the eyes of the LORD, just like his father Uzziah. Good start, friend. GOOD start.

cards.question: Jotham follows his father Uzziah in doing right. But there's one place Uzziah went that Jotham does not enter. Where?
King Jotham does right before the LORD, but the people of Judah still behave ___.

cards.text: Then Jotham rebuilds the Upper Gate of the house of the LORD and works extensively on the wall at the hill of Ophel. EXTENSIVELY, friend. That's a man who did NOT hit the snooze button.

cards.question: Jotham keeps building, with cities in the hill country of Judah. Out in the forests, what does he put up?

cards.text: Then the builder goes to battle. Jotham wages war against the king of the Ammonites.

cards.question: King Jotham goes to war against the king of the Ammonites. How does it end?

cards.text: And that year the Ammonites pay up: a hundred talents of silver, ten thousand cors of wheat and ten thousand cors of barley. TEN THOUSAND cors of wheat? I bake for a living, friend, and I have NEVER seen that much flour in one place.

cards.question: The Ammonites pay Jotham that same amount again in the second and third years.

cards.text: So Jotham grows powerful, and the text tells us exactly why. Lean in, friend, because this is the whole recipe right here.

answers.text: He ordered his ways before the LORD his God
He made treaties with the nations around him
He trained the largest army Judah ever had

cards.text: The rest of what Jotham did, all his wars and his ways, is written in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah. All his WARS? We heard about ONE! The rest are in that book, friend.
Twenty-five when he became king, sixteen years reigning in Jerusalem. Then Jotham rests with his fathers.

cards.question: King Jotham is buried in the City of ___.
After Jotham, his son Ahaz reigns in his place.

findings.problem: Card 1 gives away the answer to card 5. It tells the baker that Uzziah walked into the temple of the LORD. Card 5 then asks where Uzziah went that Jotham does not enter, and the right answer is the temple of the LORD.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Card 1 is a recap of the previous passage (2 Chronicles 26:16-21), which is provided for context only. It doesn't move the baker through 2 Chronicles 27:1-9. This passage doesn't start in the middle of a thought, so the opening card should set up Jotham's reign itself.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The question says "that same amount," which points back to the tribute listed on card 11. Card 11 isn't on screen anymore, so the baker can't see what amount is meant.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The right answer stands out. It uses Bible wording ("ordered his ways before the LORD his God"), while both wrong answers are plain modern statements about politics and the military.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
